messages.subject: How to draw line chart with time format like "00:00:00"
parts:
I tried to draw line chart with the following data:

time,  count
00:00:00, 6918
01:00:00, 6036
02:00:00, 5484
03:00:00, 4644
04:00:00, 4140
05:00:00, 3441

and with the following code:

> library(ggplot2)
Loading required package: proto
Loading required package: grid
Loading required package: reshape
Loading required package: plyr
Loading required package: digest
> data <- read.csv("data.csv")
> qplot(time, count, data = data, geom = "line")

However the chart does not show the lines? Since I am a newbie, could any Guru throw any light on it?

messages.subject: Re: How to draw line chart with time format like "00:00:00"

On Thu, Dec 24, 2009 at 09:38, Bochao Liu <l...@cert.org.cn> wrote:
> However the chart does not show the lines? Since I am a newbie, could any
> Guru throw any light on it?

not a guru but I'll try.

class(data$time) should show you that R considers the time column as a
factor or as character, i.e. as discrete values, because it has no way
of knowing that they are times on its own. Since they are discrete
values, ggplot won't join them with a line. So you need to tell R that
this is in fact a continuous time scale. To do that, use as.POSIXct()
with the appropriate format and then use your qplot command. You might
then need to reformat the labels with scale_date() if you don't like
what ggplot does by default (but it usually tries to be clever about
which part of the date to show).
